position: end — or before a participle (*serially numbered*)

senses.gloss: One after another, in a series or in installments.
examples: The novel was first published *serially* in a magazine.
All the tickets are *serially* numbered.
The old computer processed the tasks *serially*, not in parallel.

senses.gloss: By seven times as much.
examples: The number of users grew *sevenfold* in two years.
Home prices in the area have risen almost *sevenfold* since 1990.
The new engine increased the plane's range *sevenfold*.

position: mid or end — mid before a participle (*severely injured*)

senses.gloss: Very badly or seriously.
examples: Two people were *severely* injured in the crash.
The storm *severely* damaged the roof.
Our budget is *severely* limited this year.

senses.gloss: Strictly or harshly.
examples: Cheating on the exam will be punished *severely*.
The judge spoke *severely* to the young man.

senses.gloss: In a very plain style, with no decoration.
examples: She was dressed *severely* in a black suit.
Her hair was pulled back *severely* into a bun.

position: before its word — usually before an adjective or participle

senses.gloss: In a way that relates to sex.
examples: Some infections are *sexually* transmitted.
The survey asked teenagers whether they were *sexually* active.
She reported that she had been *sexually* harassed at work.

position: end — or before a participle (*shabbily dressed*)

senses.gloss: In old, worn or poor-looking clothes or condition.
examples: A *shabbily* dressed man asked us for change.
The hotel lobby was *shabbily* furnished.

senses.gloss: Unfairly or without respect.
examples: I think the company treated her very *shabbily*.
After twenty years of service, he was *shabbily* fired by email.

senses.gloss: In an unsteady, trembling or uncertain way.
examples: He stood up *shakily* after the fall.
"I'm fine," she said *shakily*.
The team started the season *shakily* but finished strong.

senses.gloss: Not deeply.
examples: The patient was breathing *shallowly*.
Plant the seeds *shallowly*, about a quarter inch down.
The book treats a serious topic rather *shallowly*.

senses.gloss: In an embarrassed way that shows you feel ashamed.
examples: He grinned *shamefacedly* and admitted he had forgotten.
The kids *shamefacedly* returned the candy they had taken.
She looked down *shamefacedly* when the teacher called her name.

position: end — or before an adjective (*shamefully low*)

senses.gloss: In a way that deserves shame or disgrace.
examples: The veterans were treated *shamefully* when they came home.
Teachers in the state are *shamefully* underpaid.
He behaved *shamefully* at his brother's wedding.

senses.gloss: Without feeling any shame or embarrassment.
examples: The ad *shamelessly* copies a famous movie scene.
He flirted *shamelessly* with every waitress.
I'm going to *shamelessly* ask you all to buy my book.

senses.gloss: In an embarrassed way, usually after a silly mistake.
examples: He smiled *sheepishly* and said he'd locked his keys in the car.
"I forgot your birthday," she admitted *sheepishly*.
The dog looked up *sheepishly* from the torn pillow.

senses.gloss: In a way that looks dishonest or suspicious, often avoiding people's eyes.
examples: The man glanced *shiftily* around the parking lot before opening the trunk.
He answered the detective's questions *shiftily*.
Her eyes moved *shiftily* from the door to the window.

position: before its word — or front as a comment on the whole sentence
modifies: adjectives and adverbs; a whole clause

senses.gloss: To a surprising and upsetting degree.
examples: The food was *shockingly* expensive.
A *shockingly* high number of students drop out in the first year.
The movie was *shockingly* bad.

senses.gloss: Used to say that a fact is surprising or upsetting.
examples: *Shockingly*, nobody was hurt in the explosion.
*Shockingly*, the report was never made public.

position: end — or before a participle (*shoddily built*)

senses.gloss: Badly and carelessly made or done.
examples: The houses were *shoddily* built and fell apart within years.
The repair was done *shoddily*, and the leak came back.
The case was *shoddily* investigated from the start.

contrast: Written without hyphens after a verb (*stand shoulder to shoulder*); hyphenated before a noun, where it is an adjective (*a shoulder-to-shoulder crowd*).

senses.gloss: Side by side and close together; also, united in support of each other.
examples: Fans stood *shoulder to shoulder* in the packed stadium.
Volunteers worked *shoulder to shoulder* to fill sandbags.
The two parties stood *shoulder to shoulder* against the new law.

senses.gloss: In a clever, practical way that shows good judgment.
examples: She *shrewdly* bought the land before prices went up.
He looked at me *shrewdly*, as if he knew I was lying.
The company invested its profits *shrewdly*.

senses.gloss: In a high, loud and unpleasant voice or sound.
examples: The whistle blew *shrilly*.
"Get out of my kitchen!" she screamed *shrilly*.
Critics complained *shrilly* about the new tax.

senses.gloss: In a nervous, timid way around other people.
examples: The little girl smiled *shyly* from behind her mother.
He *shyly* asked her to dance.
"Thank you," she said *shyly*.

type: stance — the writer's note that a mistake is quoted exactly
position: after its word — in square brackets inside a quotation
modifies: the quoted word or phrase just before it
contrast: Latin for 'thus'. It says the mistake belongs to the original, not to the person quoting it. Not the verb *sic* (*sic the dog on someone*, натравить).

senses.gloss: Written exactly this way in the original, mistake included.
examples: The sign in the window read "Open Sundy's [*sic*]."
In his letter he said he was "very greatful [*sic*] for the help."
The memo stated that the meeting was "definately [*sic*] on Friday."

position: before its word — or end after a verb

senses.gloss: In a way that makes you feel sick; to an unpleasant degree.
examples: The frosting was *sickeningly* sweet.
The car lurched *sickeningly* toward the edge of the cliff.
They're *sickeningly* cheerful first thing in the morning.

contrast: As a noun, *a sidearm* is a pistol worn at the side (*police officers carry sidearms*).

senses.gloss: With the arm moving to the side, level with the shoulder or lower, not over the head.
examples: The relief pitcher throws *sidearm*.
She skipped the stone *sidearm* across the pond.
He dropped down and threw *sidearm* to first base.

senses.gloss: Sitting with both legs on one side of a horse, bike or other seat.
examples: In old photos, women often rode *sidesaddle*.
She sat *sidesaddle* on the back of his motorcycle.
The actress learned to ride *sidesaddle* for the film.

senses.gloss: So much that you laugh very hard.
examples: The show was *sidesplittingly* funny.
He told a *sidesplittingly* funny story about his first job.
Her impressions of our boss are *sidesplittingly* accurate.

position: mid or end — before a comparative (*significantly better*); front as a comment
modifies: verbs, comparatives and adjectives; a whole clause

senses.gloss: By a large or noticeable amount.
examples: Prices have risen *significantly* since last year.
The new model is *significantly* faster.
Exercise can *significantly* reduce the risk of heart disease.

senses.gloss: Used to say that a fact is important or tells you something.
examples: *Significantly*, the mayor did not attend the meeting.
More *significantly*, the drug had no serious side effects.

senses.gloss: In a way that suggests a hidden meaning.
examples: She looked *significantly* at her husband.
He paused *significantly* before answering.

senses.gloss: Without speaking or making any sound.
examples: We sat *silently* and waited for the news.
The door slid open *silently*.
She *silently* read the letter twice.

senses.gloss: At the same time.
examples: The two bombs went off almost *simultaneously*.
The movie will be released *simultaneously* in theaters and online.
It's hard to listen and take notes *simultaneously*.

position: mid — before the verb; end is also possible
contrast: The letter closing is *Sincerely* or *Sincerely yours* in American English; British English prefers *Yours sincerely*.

senses.gloss: Honestly and really meaning what you say or feel.
examples: I *sincerely* hope you feel better soon.
We *sincerely* apologize for the delay.
He *sincerely* believed he was helping.

senses.gloss: Used to close a formal letter or email, before your name.
examples: *Sincerely*, Maria Lopez
End the cover letter with "*Sincerely* yours" and your full name.

contrast: *single-handed* is also used as the adverb with the same meaning (*she sailed around the world single-handed*); *single-handedly* is more common in American English.

senses.gloss: By yourself, with no help from anyone.
examples: She *single-handedly* raised four kids.
He won the game almost *single-handedly*.
You can't fix the economy *single-handedly*.

senses.gloss: With all your attention on one goal.
examples: She worked *single-mindedly* toward her medical degree.
The company is *single-mindedly* focused on profit.
He pursued the record *single-mindedly* for ten years.

senses.gloss: One at a time or one by one; separately.
examples: Guests arrived *singly* or in pairs.
The stamps can be bought *singly* or in books of twenty.
These birds usually hunt *singly*.

modifies: adjectives, often negative or unfavorable ones

senses.gloss: Extremely, to an unusual degree.
examples: The press conference was *singularly* unhelpful.
He was *singularly* unqualified for the job.
It was a *singularly* beautiful evening.

senses.gloss: By six times as much.
examples: The cost of the project increased *sixfold*.
Sales of electric bikes grew *sixfold* in five years.
The risk of injury rises *sixfold* without a helmet.

contrast: British spelling is *sceptically*.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows doubt.
examples: She raised an eyebrow *skeptically*.
Many scientists viewed the claim *skeptically*.
"You made this yourself?" he asked *skeptically*.

position: end — or before a participle (*sketchily reported*)
contrast: Informal *sketchy* also means 'suspicious, unsafe' (*a sketchy neighborhood*); *sketchily* almost always means 'without detail'.

senses.gloss: Without many details; only in a rough or incomplete way.
examples: The accident was only *sketchily* reported in the local paper.
She described her plans *sketchily*, leaving out the important parts.
Early maps showed the coastline very *sketchily*.

contrast: British spelling is *skilfully*.

senses.gloss: With skill; very well.
examples: The pilot *skillfully* landed the damaged plane.
The story is *skillfully* told.
She handled the angry customers *skillfully*.

position: before its word — before a participle (*skimpily dressed*)

senses.gloss: With very little clothing, or with too little of something.
examples: The dancers were *skimpily* dressed.
A few *skimpily* clad tourists were shivering on the beach.
The report was *skimpily* researched.

contrast: Before a noun it is an adjective: *sky-high prices*.

senses.gloss: Very high, or to a very high level.
examples: Rents in the city have shot *sky-high*.
The explosion blew the roof *sky-high*.
After the win, the team's confidence soared *sky-high*.

senses.gloss: Up toward the sky.
examples: The rocket rose *skyward*.
She pointed *skyward* at the eagle.
Gas prices are heading *skyward* again.

senses.gloss: Too closely, without any independent thought.
examples: The remake *slavishly* copies the original film.
Don't follow the recipe *slavishly* — taste as you go.
He *slavishly* does whatever his boss says.

position: before its word — before a participle (*sleekly designed*); also end

senses.gloss: In a smooth, elegant and modern-looking way.
examples: The new phone is *sleekly* designed, with no buttons on the front.
The car's roof curves *sleekly* toward the back.
She wore her hair *sleekly* pulled back.

senses.gloss: In a tired way, as if almost asleep.
examples: "What time is it?" he asked *sleepily*.
She rubbed her eyes *sleepily*.
The cat stretched *sleepily* in the sun.

position: before its word — before a participle (*slickly produced*); also end

senses.gloss: In a smooth, polished way, sometimes too polished to seem sincere.
examples: The ad was *slickly* produced but said very little.
The campaign was *slickly* run from start to finish.
He answered the questions *slickly*, without really answering them.

position: end — or before a participle (*sloppily written*)

senses.gloss: Carelessly, without enough attention or effort.
examples: The report was *sloppily* written and full of errors.
He dresses *sloppily* even for important meetings.
The paint was applied *sloppily* around the windows.

contrast: The comparative is *more slowly* or informal *slower*, never *slowlier*. Flat *slow* is informal and goes only after the verb (*drive slow*); before the verb use *slowly* (*She slowly opened the door*).

senses.gloss: At a low speed; not quickly.
examples: Please speak more *slowly*.
She *slowly* opened the door.
The line was moving *slowly*.

senses.gloss: Gradually, little by little over time.
examples: The economy is *slowly* recovering.
*Slowly* but surely, the kids got used to their new school.

senses.gloss: Slowly and with little energy.
examples: The river moved *sluggishly* in the heat.
My old laptop runs *sluggishly* these days.
The stock market opened *sluggishly* on Monday.

senses.gloss: In a clever, secretive or playfully knowing way.
examples: She smiled *slyly* and said nothing.
He *slyly* slipped the cookie into his pocket.
The movie *slyly* pokes fun at Hollywood.

position: before its word — before a preposition or adverb (*smack in the middle*)
modifies: prepositional phrases and adverbs such as *into*, *in the middle*
form: flat — the same form as the noun and verb *smack*
contrast: Informal. *smack-dab* is a common American variant: *smack-dab in the middle of town*.

senses.gloss: Exactly or directly, often with force.
examples: The restaurant is *smack* in the middle of downtown.
He ran *smack* into a glass door.
Our vacation fell *smack* in the middle of hurricane season.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective *small*
contrast: Mostly in fixed phrases: *start small*, *think small*, *write small*. *small* before a noun (*a small car*) is the adjective.

senses.gloss: In a small size or on a small scale.
examples: It's smart to start *small* and grow the business over time.
Don't think *small* — aim for the top.
Can you write a little *smaller* so it fits on the card?

position: before its word — before a participle (*smartly dressed*); also end

senses.gloss: In a neat, stylish way.
examples: He was *smartly* dressed in a gray suit.
The lobby is *smartly* decorated in black and white.

senses.gloss: Cleverly and sensibly.
examples: The app is *smartly* designed and easy to use.
She *smartly* decided to wait until prices dropped.
The coach *smartly* used his time-outs at the end of the game.

senses.gloss: Without problems or difficulties.
examples: The move went more *smoothly* than we expected.
Everything is running *smoothly* at the new office.
We want the transition to go *smoothly*.

senses.gloss: With an even, steady movement.
examples: The car shifts gears *smoothly*.
The skater glided *smoothly* across the ice.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you are too pleased with yourself.
examples: "I told you so," she said *smugly*.
He smiled *smugly* when his team scored.
They sat back *smugly*, sure they had won the argument.

senses.gloss: In a secret, slightly dishonest way.
examples: He *sneakily* ate the last piece of cake.
The fee was *sneakily* added to the bill.
She glanced *sneakily* at her phone during the meeting.

senses.gloss: In an unkind, indirectly insulting way.
examples: "Nice haircut," he said *snidely*.
One critic *snidely* called the film a two-hour commercial.
She remarked *snidely* that some people never do any work.

senses.gloss: In a way that treats other people as inferior.
examples: The waiter looked at our shoes *snobbishly*.
She *snobbishly* refused to shop anywhere but the most expensive stores.
He talked *snobbishly* about "real" coffee.

position: end — also before a participle (*snugly wrapped*)

senses.gloss: Closely and tightly, with no space left over.
examples: The lid fits *snugly* on the jar.
Make sure the helmet fits *snugly*.

senses.gloss: Warmly and comfortably.
examples: The baby was *snugly* wrapped in a blanket.
The cabin sits *snugly* in a valley.

contrast: Informal. Before a noun it is an adjective: *a so-so movie*.

senses.gloss: Not very well and not very badly.
examples: "How did the interview go?" "*So-so*."
Business has been going *so-so* this year.
The team played *so-so* in the first half.

senses.gloss: Completely, used in *soaking wet*.
examples: I got caught in the rain and came home *soaking* wet.
The towels are still *soaking* wet.
By the end of the water fight, everyone was *soaking* wet.

senses.gloss: In a serious, calm and sensible way.
examples: We need to think *soberly* about the risks.
The president spoke *soberly* about the losses.

senses.gloss: In plain, dark colors, with no bright decoration.
examples: The mourners were *soberly* dressed in black.
The office is *soberly* furnished in gray and brown.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; also front
modifies: adjectives and participles; a whole clause

senses.gloss: In terms of income, education and social class.
examples: The program helps students from *socioeconomically* disadvantaged families.
The neighborhood is racially and *socioeconomically* diverse.
*Socioeconomically*, the two groups were very similar.

position: front — or before an adjective (*sociologically interesting*)

senses.gloss: From the point of view of sociology, the study of society.
examples: *Sociologically* speaking, the suburbs changed American family life.
The rise of online dating is *sociologically* fascinating.
The study is *sociologically* important but hard to read.

senses.gloss: Quietly, not loudly.
examples: She spoke *softly* so she wouldn't wake the baby.
Music played *softly* in the background.
Rain was falling *softly* on the roof.

senses.gloss: Gently, with little force.
examples: He *softly* touched her arm.
Knock *softly* — Grandpa is sleeping.
The room was *softly* lit by candles.

senses.gloss: In a very serious and formal way.
examples: I *solemnly* swear to tell the truth.
The boy nodded *solemnly*.
The crowd stood *solemnly* for a moment of silence.

senses.gloss: In a caring way that shows concern for someone's comfort or health.
examples: "Are you warm enough?" the nurse asked *solicitously*.
He hovered *solicitously* around his pregnant wife.
The staff treated the older guests *solicitously*.

position: end — or before a participle or adjective (*solidly built*, *solidly Democratic*)

senses.gloss: Firmly and strongly; reliably well.
examples: The old barn is *solidly* built.
The team played *solidly* all season.

senses.gloss: Completely and consistently, with no break or exception.
examples: The county has voted *solidly* Republican for decades.
It rained *solidly* for three days.
The staff is *solidly* behind the new plan.

contrast: Also a noun (*a guitar solo*) and an adjective (*a solo album*). *Go solo* means leave a band or group to work alone.

senses.gloss: Alone, without anyone else.
examples: She flew *solo* for the first time at sixteen.
He left the band in 2015 to go *solo*.
I like traveling *solo*.

contrast: British spelling is *sombrely*.

senses.gloss: In a sad, serious or dark way.
examples: The families waited *somberly* for news of the miners.
"There's nothing more we can do," the doctor said *somberly*.
The guests were *somberly* dressed in dark suits.

position: before its word — before a number; end in the informal sense
contrast: Before a noun *some* is a determiner (*some water*). As an adverb it means 'about' before a number. The end-position use (*rest some*) is informal American speech, not written English.

senses.gloss: About, approximately, before a number.
examples: The fire destroyed *some* 200 homes.
The village is *some* ten miles from the coast.
*Some* forty percent of voters stayed home.

senses.gloss: To some degree; a little (informal American).
examples: I need to rest *some* before we keep going.
It's warmed up *some* since this morning.

modifies: verbs; takes *else* and an adjective after it (*someplace quiet*)
contrast: Informal American for *somewhere*. Like *somewhere*, it takes an adjective after it: *someplace warm*, not *warm someplace*.

senses.gloss: In or to a place that is not named or known.
examples: Let's go *someplace* quiet to talk.
I left my keys *someplace* in the kitchen.
They moved *someplace* in Arizona.

modifies: verbs; often followed by a time phrase (*sometime next week*)
contrast: *sometime* (at some point) is not *sometimes* (occasionally), and neither is *some time* (a period of time): *Call me sometime*; *I sometimes call her*; *It took some time*.

senses.gloss: At a time that is not known or not stated, in the past or future.
examples: Let's have lunch *sometime*.
The house was built *sometime* in the 1920s.
I'll call you *sometime* next week.

senses.gloss: In a calm way that makes someone feel less upset or in less pain.
examples: "It's okay, you're safe now," she said *soothingly*.
He talked *soothingly* to the frightened horse.
The music was *soothingly* quiet.

senses.gloss: Completely, used in *sopping wet*.
examples: My socks were *sopping* wet after the walk through the field.
The dog came in from the rain *sopping* wet.
Don't leave that *sopping* wet towel on the bed.

position: mid — before a participle or verb (*sorely needed*)

senses.gloss: Very much; badly.
examples: The town is *sorely* in need of a new hospital.
Your help was *sorely* missed.
I was *sorely* tempted to quit on the spot.

senses.gloss: With deep feeling, often sad feeling.
examples: She sang the old hymn *soulfully*.
The dog gazed *soulfully* at my sandwich.
A saxophone played *soulfully* on the street corner.

senses.gloss: Without making any sound.
examples: The cat moved *soundlessly* across the floor.
Her lips moved *soundlessly* as she read.
The door swung *soundlessly* open.

position: end — or before a participle (*soundly based*)

senses.gloss: Deeply, of sleep.
examples: The kids were sleeping *soundly* when we got home.
I slept *soundly* for the first time in weeks.

senses.gloss: Completely and clearly, of a defeat.
examples: The incumbent was *soundly* defeated in the election.
We got beaten *soundly* in the final.

senses.gloss: Sensibly and reliably, on a good basis.
examples: The argument is *soundly* based on the evidence.
The money was *soundly* invested.

senses.gloss: In an unfriendly, bad-tempered or disappointed way.
examples: "Great, another meeting," he said *sourly*.
She looked *sourly* at the pile of dishes.
Fans reacted *sourly* to the trade.

contrast: As an adverb it takes no preposition: *drive south*, *fly south*, not *drive to south*. Use *to the south* or *in the south* when it is a noun. *down south* is common in American speech, often meaning the Southern states: *My grandparents live down south*.

senses.gloss: Toward or in the south.
senses.ru: на юг, к югу, на юге
examples: Many birds fly *south* for the winter.
We drove *south* on I-95.
The airport is about twenty miles *south* of the city.

form: south + east, written as one word in American English

senses.gloss: Toward or in the southeast.
examples: The hurricane is moving *southeast*, away from the coast.
The town is fifteen miles *southeast* of Atlanta.
Turn *southeast* at the next intersection.

form: south + west, written as one word in American English

senses.gloss: Toward or in the southwest.
examples: We drove *southwest* toward the desert.
The ranch lies forty miles *southwest* of Tucson.
The trail heads *southwest* from the parking lot.

senses.gloss: In small amounts; not much or not often.
examples: Use the hot sauce *sparingly* — it's really strong.
The coach uses his young players *sparingly*.
Water the plant *sparingly* in winter.

position: before its word — before a participle (*sparsely populated*)

senses.gloss: With only a few people or things spread over an area.
examples: Wyoming is the most *sparsely* populated state.
The apartment was *sparsely* furnished.
The early show was *sparsely* attended.

senses.gloss: Now and then, not regularly or continuously.
examples: He worked on the book only *spasmodically*.
Fighting continued *spasmodically* through the night.

senses.gloss: With sudden movements of the muscles that you cannot control.
examples: His leg twitched *spasmodically*.
The fish flapped *spasmodically* on the deck.

senses.gloss: In terms of space, size or position.
examples: Some people are *spatially* gifted and can read maps easily.
The data were mapped *spatially* across the country.
The two buildings are *spatially* close but feel very different.

position: before its word — before a participle (*specially designed*); also end
contrast: *specially* mainly means 'for a particular purpose' (*specially made*). For 'above all, particularly' the standard word is *especially* (*I love fruit, especially apples*); *specially* in that sense is informal speech.

senses.gloss: For a particular purpose or person.
examples: The kitchen was *specially* designed for a wheelchair user.
I made this cake *specially* for you.
The trucks are *specially* equipped for snow.

senses.gloss: Particularly; more than usual (informal).
examples: It's a *specially* hard time of year for us.
He's not *specially* interested in sports.

position: end — or before an adjective (*spectacularly beautiful*)

senses.gloss: In a very impressive or dramatic way; to a very great degree.
examples: The plan failed *spectacularly*.
The canyon is *spectacularly* beautiful at sunset.
Her first business succeeded *spectacularly*.
